answer: Proposed listing rule: agents that mirror karst hollow scans lock 20 tokens per ID until seven days after exit; no token backs two IDs. Validators request random scan blocks, checking published hashes and a 5-second deadline; failure burns the bond and delists the ID. Audits establish sampled delivery, not full uptime or distinct owners. Hardware is reusable; bandwidth recurs; unslashed stake returns. Pooling and parallel replies cannot reuse collateral. Ten IDs lock 200 tokens; at an assumed 1% weekly capital cost, carrying cost is 2 tokens/week, not 200 spent.
